back: A coordinator decomposes work, delegates to specialized agents and aggregates results (hub-and-spoke).
Agents in a chain; each stage consumes the previous output (planner > implementer > tester > reviewer).
Many agents work independently at once, then results are merged.
One agent produces, another critiques, looping until criteria are met.
Agents react to GitHub events such as labels or issue creation.

front: How do you isolate parallel agents?
back: Separate branches/sessions/worktrees/environments with disjoint file ownership; share only via commits and artifacts.
Overlapping code changes, duplicated effort, contradictory outputs.
Serialize, rebase, re-partition ownership, or integrate via an integrator agent/human.
Claim work before starting (assignment, label, sub-issue) and check existing claims.
Escalate to an arbiter (human or designated agent) and record the decision in one place.

front: What goes in a hand-off record?
back: Who handed what (inputs, outputs, assumptions) to whom, plus decisions and why.

front: Artifacts that make multi-agent work auditable?
back: One PR per agent task, linked issues, session logs, scan results, decision log.
Session logs, commit co-author trails, audit log events, PR/issue timelines.
Failed, partial, stalled, degraded.
Detect via timeout/heartbeat; cancel, roll back partial work, re-queue or escalate.
Resume from a checkpoint idempotently or roll back; do not restart blindly.
Stop routing work to an agent that keeps failing/degrading; fall back to a human or alternative while investigating.

front: Safely add an agent to a live workflow?
back: Define role, tools and hand-off contract; review its definition via PR; pilot on low-risk tasks.

front: Safely update or replace an agent?
back: Version definitions, roll out gradually, drain or hand off in-flight work, keep hand-off contracts backward compatible.
Stop new routing, finish/reassign in-flight work, preserve logs/PRs/decision records, document the replacement.
